name: Lip reduction surgery

lead: Lip reduction removes tissue so very full lips become smaller and sit in better balance with the rest of the face. The smaller lips are visible once healed.

Strips of tissue are excised, usually from the inner lip, so the scar sits inside the mouth. The literature mostly covers it for medical conditions such as macrocheilia from vascular malformations, granulomatous cheilitis and Van der Woude syndrome. A 2000 series of 66 patients found lip reduction far less common than enlargement, and a 2007 technique called bikini lip reduction was described for hypertrophic lips.

paras: A surgeon performs it as an operation, with healing over a few weeks. Interest in the cosmetic version is small compared with lip enlargement, and it is reported in places where thinner lips are preferred.
The change is permanent. Scarring and asymmetry are general surgical concerns, and cosmetic-specific outcome data are scarce.

angle.text: Lip reduction is used by people who feel very full lips are out of balance with the rest of the face, with smaller lips visible after healing. The literature covers it mainly for medical conditions such as macrocheilia, with little cosmetic research.

lead: Lip reduction surgery, or reduction cheiloplasty, removes tissue from the lips to make them smaller. People choose it to bring thick or protruding lips into proportion with the rest of the face and to balance the upper and lower lip; the surgical literature also describes it for medical conditions such as macrocheilia from vascular malformations, granulomatous cheilitis and Van der Woude syndrome [1][2][3][4][5][6].

A 2025 article in Facial Plastic Surgery describes lip reduction as a low-risk, relatively quick in-office procedure, using an elliptical incision at the wet-dry border and removal of mucosa [7]. A 2010 review by Joseph Niamtu, drawing on 26 years of experience, calls it predictable and safe with high patient acceptance when diagnostic and treatment criteria are followed, and says it is used primarily in ethnic populations [1][1]. Named techniques include the 'bikini lip reduction' [8][9], a 'Brazilian' variant [10] and the 'crab claw' approach [11].

A 2000 series of 66 patients found lip reduction in 7 of 86 procedures, with lip enlargement far more common [12]. Grokipedia says lip reduction is done in places such as South Korea and Thailand to meet preferences for thinner lips, which is unverified [13]. In looksmaxxing forums the topic is discussed less often than lip filler, because fuller lips are frequently regarded as attractive, but threads do ask whether lips are too large for a given face [14].
infobox: Inside the lip, at the wet-dry border [8][7]
Can be done in the office [7]
Up to about two weeks in one series [9]
May take up to two years as lips continue to shrink [9]

paras: Techniques remove an elliptical strip of mucosa and underlying tissue from inside the lip, hiding the scar in the mouth [8][1]. Other approaches such as an inverted-T excision treat the lower lip in Van der Woude syndrome [2].

The main idea is to reduce volume while restoring a natural contour and proportion. In the 'bikini' technique, surgeons describe marking and removing a shape from the upper lip, resembling a bikini top, and a triangular piece from the lower lip, aiming to keep the lower lip about 40 to 50 percent larger than the upper [9]. Closure uses absorbable sutures, and preserving the corners of the mouth is emphasised [9].

Fanous, Brousseau and Yoskovitch described the bikini lip reduction in 2007 in 11 patients aged 22 to 48, who were mostly women; they reported universal swelling for up to two weeks, minimal pain, scars that healed in three to six months and no significant complications, though they offer no formal outcome measures [9]. In 2012 Sforza and colleagues presented a 'Brazilian' bikini-shaped technique performed in more than 40 patients between 2008 and 2010, with a more conservative upper resection and curved lower resection, and reported no infections or other complications [10].

In 2020 a nine-patient case series of the 'crab claw' technique, a modified incision meant to reduce volume while keeping a typical Indian lip appearance, reported about 10 mm less lip width at the midline at six months, no complications and satisfaction in all patients [11]. For Van der Woude syndrome, a review of 34 patients with lower-lip pits found that inverted-T lip reduction scored best on aesthetic results from professional and lay raters [2]. A 2024 case report describes Conway's method with lateral wedge excisions for granulomatous cheilitis after four years of unsuccessful medical therapy [6].

The 2025 article describes ideal candidates as people with large upper or lower lips who want less volume, and describes postoperative care including a soft diet for one week, activity restriction for two weeks and frequent petrolatum-based ointment [7]. Niamtu's review focuses on cosmetic reduction of enlarged lips, particularly in ethnic populations, and Lam's 2005 review of aesthetic facial surgery for Asian men lists lip reduction among procedures discussed [1][15]. A 1987 review of non-Caucasian rhinoplasty includes adjunctive reduction cheiloplasty [16].

Lip procedures divide into enlargement and reduction. Fillers and lip lift surgery are the most common cosmetic lip procedures [7]. Wikipedia lists labial frenectomy, lip augmentation and lip lift as related cheiloplasty procedures [17]. A Google Trends study compared search volumes for facial cosmetic procedures, including lip augmentation and lip reduction, with U.S. surgical volumes [18].

A 2000 series of 66 patients reported seven lip reductions among 86 procedures [12]. Case reports and reviews cover reduction for Van der Woude syndrome lower lip pits [2][3], granulomatous macrocheilitis in childhood [4] and hypertrophic upper lip in vascular malformations [5]. A registered trial in the source list studies lip reduction for port-wine macrocheilia, 60 participants [19]. Studies on purely cosmetic reduction are scarce.

A 2020 case series of nine patients reported lip width falling by about 10 mm at six months [11]. A series of more than 40 patients treated with a bikini-shaped technique and an 11-patient bikini series reported no significant complications [9][10]. These are small case series without control groups, and no randomized trial of cosmetic lip reduction has been published.
Threads on looksmax.org ask whether lips are too large for a face; replies often state that full lips are attractive and that reduction is not needed [14].

In one thread, a reply says a slight reduction of an upper lip could suit a white man, while another says full lips are attractive and the money could be spent elsewhere [14]. Interest in lip surgery more broadly is tracked in search-trend research [18].

Reported effects across the series include swelling, mucosal scars and, as with any lip surgery, possible asymmetry and loss of volume that cannot be restored by simple means [9][7]. Reductions are permanent, and the 2007 authors note lips can continue to shrink for up to two years [9].

lore.intro: Lip reduction comes up occasionally on looksmax.org, where most replies favour fuller lips.[14]

claims.claim: Very full lips can hurt facial harmony and may merit reduction.
Full lips are attractive, so reduction is rarely needed.
Lip reduction is a quick, low-risk procedure.
